reply:
Still `typeof null` returns `'object'`. Because that's what every JavaScript engine does—V8 (Chrome, Node), SpiderMonkey (Firefox), JavaScriptCore (Safari), all of them.

ES6 did not change this. No ECMAScript version has changed it. There were proposals to fix it, but it was kept for backward compatibility. Test it in any modern Node or browser console:

```
typeof null  // 'object'
```

What would change my mind: a link to the spec or a working engine that returns something else.

The concrete cost of being wrong here: your code skips the null check and silently treats null as an object, leading to bugs like `null.property` crashing later.

Guard it: `v !== null && typeof v === 'object'`.
